items.title: The belonging word changes the relationship
items.caption: The surrounding words stay the same. The choice between *a* and *o* decides whether the house was built by the boy or is his home.

states.label: Built by him
states.sm: ʻO le fale a le tama.

states.label: His home
states.sm: ʻO le fale o le tama.
states.en: The boy's house (the house he lives in).

items.title: Possessive forms in two columns
items.caption: Each person has an *a*-word form and an *o*-word form. The thing possessed decides the column.

items.title: Sort the things by belonging type
items.intro: Place each printed word under the belonging word used with it in this chapter.

items.why: A knife is acquired and put to use, so the chapter prints it with *a*.
A car is acquired and put to use, so the chapter prints it with *a*.
The chapter lists a cup among the things acquired and put to use.
A head is part of the person, so the chapter prints it with *o*.
A hand is part of the person, so the chapter prints it with *o*.
A leg or foot is part of the person, so the chapter prints it with *o*.
